# Phase 3 prompt — Make the full workflow inspectable and improve information architecture

Implement only Phase 3 of the Unfinished Business roadmap. Make Oracle, Architect, Maker, and Witness pages inspectable at any time while preserving workflow gates for mutations. Replace technical outlines with clear user-facing project sections.

## Prerequisite

Verify Phase 1 provides durable runs and Phase 2 provides a working OpenCode connection state. Do not hide unresolved run or connection failures behind new navigation.

## Outcome

Users can understand the whole journey, inspect completed/current/future stages, return to their active task, and see which project sections are ready, stale, locked, or blocked. Viewing a stage must never be mistaken for approval or authorization to execute it.

## Inspect before editing

- Inspect existing stage state, route handling, workflow guards, approval/version logic, section schema, saved project migration, and responsive UI.
- Identify every place where the current stage and selected view are conflated.
- Preserve stable internal IDs and hashes when changing labels.
- Inspect prompt-loading assumptions so repository implementation prompts never appear as runtime spirit prompts.

## Work to perform

- Separate `active workflow stage` from `selected UI tab`.
- Make all four spirit tabs selectable:
  - completed stages show approved artifacts and evidence;
  - the active stage allows permitted actions;
  - future stages show purpose, prerequisites, expected output, and preview;
  - mutations remain server-authorized and disabled until prerequisites pass.
- Persist the selected tab in a shareable URL or route without changing the active workflow state.
- Add a visible active-stage badge, progress summary, blockers, and “Return to active task.”
- Prevent tab changes, refreshes, or direct URLs from granting approvals, execution scope, or permission.
- Replace current user-facing section names with:
  1. Vision & Success
  2. Architecture
  3. User Experience
  4. OpenCode Setup
  5. Tools & Budget
  6. Validation
  7. Build Roadmap
  8. Demo & Launch
- Retain stable internal identifiers and migrate existing saved records without invalidating valid approvals solely because display labels changed.
- Give each section a status, concise summary, dependencies, last update, stale reason, evidence/approval link, and clear edit/review action.
- Add a project overview containing readiness, active blockers, current run, OpenCode state, budget/tool status, demo status, and next action.
- Improve loading, empty, locked, stale, partial, error, and recovery states.
- Ensure keyboard, focus, landmarks, narrow layout, overflow, and reduced-motion behavior are usable.

## Tests

Cover selected-tab versus active-stage separation, direct URLs, reload persistence, future-tab read-only behavior, server-side mutation gates, section-label migration, stale dependencies, accessibility navigation, and responsive rendering. Include a regression proving that viewing Maker or Witness cannot activate them.

## Documentation requirements

Update:

- `docs/PRODUCT_BRIEF.md` for the refined user journey and terminology;
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for selected-view versus workflow-state ownership;
- `docs/UX_AND_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md` for navigation, section anatomy, states, responsive behavior, and accessibility;
- `docs/OPERATIONS_AND_RECOVERY.md` for stale/blocked state recovery;
- `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `docs/CHANGELOG.md`, and `README.md`.

Update runtime prompt or schema documentation only where section labels or dependencies actually change. Do not rename the four runtime prompt source files in this phase unless a tested loader migration is included and necessary.

## Acceptance

- All four stages are inspectable before generation finishes.
- Only the active authorized stage can mutate state.
- Direct navigation cannot bypass approval gates.
- Existing approved sections survive display-name migration.
- Users can identify the current task and next action from every stage.
- Narrow/wide, keyboard, focus, and reduced-motion checks pass.
- Tests, typecheck, and build pass; docs use the same terminology as the UI.

Finish with the required phase handoff and stop. Do not start Phase 4.
I'll start by inspecting the repository structure and current state before making changes.

# Unfinished Business

**Bring your ideas to life.**

A local browser companion built on OpenCode's open-source coding harness. Four friendly spirits guide a builder from an unfinished idea through an approved plan, real implementation, verification, and submission drafts.

| Spirit | Role |
|---|---|
| Oracle | Clarify an idea and approve a useful product scope |
| Architect | Present one planning section, revise it, and wait for approval before continuing |
| Maker | Use OpenCode to perform approved work and show actual results |
| Witness | Review evidence and prepare honest final materials |

OpenCode provides the agent loop, model access, tools, permissions, and native sessions. Unfinished Business adds the workshop interface, stage progression, versioned approvals, decision history, and evidence views.

## Status

Prompt 2 is active. Foundation is `14fc6a6`, Workflow is `abf87f7`, and Experience is `b465fa0`. The Verification phase has entered local reconciliation: typecheck, production build, all 21 tests, and the production dependency audit pass. Oracle, Architect, Maker, and Witness run through OpenCode's free DeepSeek route. Maker edits only an isolated demo workspace, then the app runs `node --test` there. A live umbrella-relay attempt wrote a ledger whose Node check failed on a duplicate `snapshot` declaration; Witness recorded that failure. Sentry error, performance, replay, feedback, profiling, and metadata-only OpenCode agent tracing are verified locally. Backboard remains dependent on its API/tooling setup.

```bash
npm ci
npm run dev
```

In another terminal, `npm run build && npm start` serves the built workshop and API on `127.0.0.1`. Set `UB_PORT` if `4200` is taken. `OPENCODE_BASE_URL` defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:4096`. The server scripts and Vite read the gitignored `.env`; use `.env.example` as the safe template. Start `opencode serve` yourself; this app does not print or store its password. Project data stays in `UB_DATA_DIR` (default `.unfinished-business/`), which is gitignored.

Environment setup, Sentry release/source-map configuration, and OpenCode password matching are documented in [docs/SENTRY_AND_OPENCODE_SETUP.md](docs/SENTRY_AND_OPENCODE_SETUP.md).

Render deployment and its required secrets are documented in [docs/RENDER_DEPLOYMENT.md](docs/RENDER_DEPLOYMENT.md). The hosted service is password protected and uses a persistent disk; it is not compatible with Render's free plan.

Run the dependency-free diagnostic from the repository:

```bash
node scripts/preflight.mjs
```

It checks the toolchain, read-only Git state, DNS, localhost socket access and Entire status. A temporary localhost listener closes immediately. OpenCode version/help use disposable temporary storage, without changing existing sessions or credentials. It performs no inference, installs, account setup, capture setup or Git writes. Exit code 1 means a blocking diagnostic failed; exit code 0 is only preflight, never a passing integration proof. See the blueprint's execution record for the tested result and resume conditions.

- [Engineering blueprint](docs/ENGINEERING_BLUEPRINT.md) — canonical implementation plan and amendments.
- [Product idea packet](docs/Unfinished-Business-Idea-Packet-v1.md) — approved product scope and updated decisions.
- [Complete local prompt set](docs/prompts/README.md) — Prompts 0–3 and current project overrides.
- [Project Prompt 1](docs/prompts/PROMPT_1_ARCHITECT.md) — complete project-specific Architect instructions with section-by-section review.

## Development policy

- Repository: [kernelKain/unfinished-business](https://github.com/kernelKain/unfinished-business).
- Work on the existing `main` branch. Do not create phase branches.
- Complete and verify each phase, then make one commit for that phase before starting the next phase.
- Steps are work/checklist units, not individual commits. Commit subjects describe the change without phase or step numbering.
- Preserve unrelated changes. A blocked commit blocks entry to the next implementation phase; do not bypass access restrictions.

The Experience gate is committed and linked to Entire checkpoint `01M6874YH3592P2RKCZ9KV0MVQ`. The active unit is Verification V1 partner access: Backboard and Sentry work waits for supported credentials/tooling or an approved focused amendment. Publication and submission belong to Prompt 3.

## Delivery

The first release targets a local browser on Linux. A real recorded demonstration and a reproducible local-start guide provide judge access; hosted code execution is outside this release. Backboard, Sentry Agent Tracing, and Entire remain selected partner targets, with qualification conditional on meaningful actual use and evidence.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). Dependency, prompt, and asset attribution must be checked before redistribution.

# Implementation Plan

Status: Phase 1 complete in the working tree, pending the phase commit.
Phase 2 has not started.

## Phase 1 objective

Replace the blocking Maker request with a durable asynchronous OpenCode run lifecycle and a user-visible Run Inspector. Reliability first; no broad visual redesign or tool recommendation work.

## Completed work

### Backend

- Added schema-versioned run records and append-only public events in `src/shared/runs.ts`.
- Added `RunStore` with a global sequence, atomic writes, previous-snapshot recovery, and run/action lookup.
- Added `RunCoordinator` with a bounded in-process queue (default concurrency 1, queue 8), lifecycle validation, timeout, cancellation observation, reconciliation, and restart recovery.
- `POST /api/runs` now validates authorization, persists `QUEUED`, returns `202` immediately, and schedules work after acknowledgement.
- Native session IDs are persisted before the prompt; message IDs are persisted immediately after the prompt call.
- Native event subscription is normalized into versioned public events. Reasoning, prompts, tool arguments, and tool results are excluded.
- Added authenticated SSE with snapshot, replay, `Last-Event-ID`/`after` cursor resume, gap resync, heartbeats, and terminal close.
- Cancellation invokes `session.interrupt`; `CANCELLED` is only written after the native outcome is observed, otherwise `UNKNOWN`.
- Timeout produces `UNKNOWN` while retaining session and message identity.

# Architecture

Unfinished Business is a browser workshop on top of OpenCode's native harness. OpenCode owns the agent loop, providers, models, tools, permissions, and sessions. The application owns the product journey, staged approvals, evidence, connection discovery, and the trust boundary around secrets.

## Runtime topology

```text
Browser (React)
  │  same-origin HTTP, optional Basic auth, X-UB-Session-Token for mutations
  ▼
Unfinished Business server (Hono)
  │  server-side Basic auth; never forwards provider credentials
  ▼
OpenCode server (loopback by default; HTTPS remotely)
  │
  ├─ OpenCode credential store / XDG data directory
  ├─ provider + model catalog
  ├─ agents, permissions, commands, skills, MCP
  └─ native sessions, diffs, usage
```

The browser never calls OpenCode directly. This avoids browser CORS/origin dependencies and keeps the OpenCode password and provider credentials out of the page. The browser receives normalized model/agent/capability facts and project state only.

## Server modules

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `src/server/app.ts` | HTTP routes, request validation, authorization guards, error mapping. |
| `src/server/index.ts` | Process composition, deployment mode, persistent paths, stale-run reconciliation. |
| `src/server/render-start.ts` | Hosted process supervision: starts OpenCode, then the app. |
| `src/server/opencode/client.ts` | Exact client construction, URL policy, version policy, error classification, redaction. |
| `src/server/opencode/connection.ts` | Connection state, settings persistence, discovery, diagnostics, model choice/validation. |
| `src/server/opencode/discovery.ts` | Pure normalization from OpenCode catalogs to product-safe facts. |
| `src/server/opencode/sessions.ts` | Project-scoped session list/resume/interrupt/fork/compact/revert/permission/usage actions. |
| `src/server/experience/guide.ts` | Thin adapter from spirit roles to native sessions and model/agent selection. |
| `src/server/experience/runs.ts` | Background Maker run lifecycle and persisted operation updates. |
| `src/server/experience/service.ts` | Journey transitions and orchestration across Oracle/Architect/Maker/Witness. |
| `src/server/workflow/*` | Durable project schema, exact approvals, invalidation, migration helpers. |
| `src/server/store/*` | Atomic JSON persistence, previous snapshot, serialized writes. |

## Persisted project (schema v2)

```jsonc
{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "revision": 0,
  "stage": "ORACLE",
  "engine": {
    "model": { "providerID": "opencode", "id": "flint-40b-free", "variant": "high" },
    "source": "user",
    "updatedAt": "2026-10-31T…",
    "legacyModel": null
  },
  "operations": [
    {
      "id": "…",
      "kind": "maker",
      "status": "SUCCEEDED",
      "model": { "providerID": "opencode", "id": "flint-40b-free", "variant": "high" },
      "agent": "build",
      "nativeSessionId": "ses_…",
      "startedAt": "…",
      "finishedAt": "…",
      "result": "…"
    }
  ],
  "evidence": [
    { "checkId": "CK-06", "result": "PASS", "model": { "providerID": "opencode", "id": "flint-40b-free" } }
  ]
}
```

- `engine.model` is the user's discovered model choice. It is not a constant.
- `engine.source` records `none`, `user`, `migrated-legacy`, or `auto-discovery`.
- Operations and evidence record the model used, so run evidence is reproducible even after a later selection change.
- `connection.json` is a separate file and contains no password.

### Migration from v1

The v1 schema was written when the code hard-coded `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`. `migrateProject()`:

1. reads a v1 document;
2. keeps every section, action, operation, evidence, and native-session reference;
3. adds `engine: { model: null, source: "migrated-legacy", legacyModel: "opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free" }`;
4. adds null model/agent/timestamps to historical operations/evidence;
5. returns schema v2.

On the next discovery, the legacy model is used only if OpenCode still reports it and it is available. Otherwise the user chooses a reported model. No unavailable model is silently substituted. A corrupt current file is preserved and the previous snapshot is offered.

## Connection state machine

```text
not_configured
  → checking
      → connected
      → degraded (untested patch, provider auth, pending permission, model issue, partial probe)
      → authentication_required (401)
      → incompatible_version (major ≠ 2 or unparseable)
      → unavailable (transport, timeout, origin/403, malformed response)
```

A check is read-only. It calls `/api/info` first, then catalog/agent/permission/command/skill/MCP/config endpoints. A failed check returns a diagnostic code and repair text; it never leaves an optimistic success status. The wizard and panel both surface the same diagnostics.

### URL and trust boundary

- `http://` is allowed only for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and `::1`.
- `https://` is allowed for any host.
- URL userinfo, query strings, and fragments are rejected.
- The server password is sent as `Authorization: Basic` from the server process. It is not sent to or stored by the browser.
- `hosted-private` and `hosted-demo` treat the connection as managed; browser configuration routes return 409.
- Provider keys are never accepted by any application route.

## Asynchronous Maker lifecycle

The Phase 1 prerequisite is the non-blocking run model used here:

1. `POST /api/runs` claims the action, validates Maker scope and the selected model, persists a `QUEUED` operation with model/agent/timestamps, starts the in-process runner, and returns `202` immediately.
2. The runner persists `RUNNING`, then the native session ID as soon as OpenCode creates it.
3. The native turn, diff, and bounded Node check run outside the HTTP request.
4. Completion is applied with `executeLatest()`, a bounded retry against the current revision, so unrelated user actions can happen while the run is in flight.
5. A process restart converts `QUEUED`/`RUNNING` operations to `UNKNOWN` with a repair note. Nothing is replayed.
6. Cancellation interrupts the native session and marks the operation `CANCELLED`; a late completion cannot overwrite that state.
7. The browser polls `/api/project` while an operation is active and renders the persisted status. It does not hold an HTTP request open for the whole run.

`AtomicProjectStore` serializes writes and uses a UUID temporary filename so two background updates cannot collide or overwrite each other silently.

## Capability-driven UI

The UI renders from discovered facts, not fixed constants:

- models, providers, variants, limits, modalities, tool support, pricing, local status;
- agents and role mapping;
- pending permissions;
- commands, skills, MCP servers, formatter/LSP configuration;
- session controls and reported usage.

Unsupported controls are visible as deferred with a reason. The main journey remains the focus; advanced controls live inside the expandable OpenCode panel.

## Trust boundaries and data handling

| Boundary | Rule |
|---|---|
| Browser → app | Basic auth when hosted; session token for mutations; no provider credentials accepted. |
| App → OpenCode | Server-side only; Basic auth password in memory or `OPENCODE_PASSWORD`; HTTPS required off loopback. |
| App → disk | Project JSON, connection metadata (no password), isolated workspaces. |
| App → logs/Sentry | Redacted error messages; no authorization headers, passwords, provider keys, or prompt bodies. |
| App → export | Approved plan, drafts, selected engine metadata; no secrets. |
| OpenCode → app catalogs | Normalized, allow-listed fields; raw provider/model/config settings are discarded. |

## Deployment modes

- `local`: wizard may configure a loopback or HTTPS URL; project data under `UB_DATA_DIR`.
- `hosted-private`: connection managed by environment/secret store; OpenCode XDG data on a persistent disk; visitors do not provide credentials.
- `hosted-demo`: connection managed and read-only; no provider-key prompts; may show `NO_MODELS` when no provider is connected.

See [HOSTED_DEPLOYMENT.md](HOSTED_DEPLOYMENT.md) for the exact environment.

## Known limitations

- OpenCode `2.0.32` has no separate HTTP tool catalog.
- Formatter/LSP status is configuration presence, not live process health.
- Quota/balance is not available via the HTTP API.
- Cost/token values depend on provider reporting.
- Other 2.x patches are degraded until the live diagnostic is run.
- Fork requires a non-empty session.
# UX and visual system

The product is a guided workshop, not a control panel. The main journey is always visible first; OpenCode configuration and harness controls live behind one expandable panel.

## Onboarding states

The first-run wizard has three visible steps: **Server**, **Model**, **Verify**.

| State | What the user sees | Primary action |
|---|---|---|
| `not_configured` | The start command, URL field, username, password field, and the provider-key ownership note. | **Test connection** |
| `checking` | Button label changes to **Checking…**; no success is implied. | Wait |
| `authentication_required` | “OpenCode rejected the application connection” plus the server-password repair, not a provider-key request. | Re-enter password / retry |
| `incompatible_version` | Exact server version, tested `2.0.32`, and a 2.x repair. | Install compatible server |
| `unavailable` | “The server did not answer” plus start/URL/port repair. | Start OpenCode, retry |
| `connected` / `degraded` | Provider readiness, full model list, limit/pricing/tool/modality facts, and only the variants reported for the chosen model. | Choose model |
| Model saved | Model and variant appear in the main journey’s **Run model** panel and in the OpenCode panel. | Continue journey |
| Wizard dismissed | The journey is visible with a connection/model banner; Maker stays blocked until setup is repaired. | **Choose model** / **Open setup** |

### Copy rules

- Say **OpenCode server password**, never “API key”.
- State clearly that provider keys stay in OpenCode and that the workshop cannot accept them.
- A failure names the exact state and gives one repair path. Do not say “something went wrong”.
- A model is never called “free” unless every reported cost row is zero.
- A model is never given a generic low/medium/high scale. Variants are exactly the reported IDs, plus **Model default**.
- Usage is shown only when reported; otherwise say “not reported”, not `0`.
- Quota is not available programmatically; link to the provider console and say so.

## Main journey

The existing spirit strip, lantern, outline, working document, and activity/evidence sidebars remain. New information is deliberately small:

- A **Run model** panel in the left sidebar shows the selected model, variant, pricing, tool support, context, and local status.
- Connection problems appear as a banner above the working document with **Open setup** or **Review**.
- An active run appears as a banner saying it is working in the background, with **Cancel run**. The saved document is not replaced by a blocking spinner.
- An unselected or disappeared model blocks Maker with an explicit **Choose model** action. No silent substitution.
- The top bar has an **OpenCode** button for the connection wizard.

## Advanced OpenCode panel

One `<details>` disclosure, collapsed by default, labelled **OpenCode settings and controls**. Sections:

1. **Status** — state pill, URL, version, managed/local, refresh, connection setup, diagnostics.
2. **Model and reasoning** — discovered models grouped by provider, variant list for the chosen model, pricing/limits/tools/modality/locality, **Save model**.
3. **Agents, roles, and permissions** — Oracle/Architect/Maker/Witness mapping with explicit fallback; visible agents; pending requests with **Allow once**, **Always**, **Reject**.
4. **Discovered harness capabilities** — supported/deferred matrix with a reason for each deferred item; commands, skills, MCP, formatter/LSP configuration.
5. **Usage, tokens, and cost** — only reported totals; quota explanation and provider links.
6. **Project sessions** — list/resume, fork (disabled when empty), compact, interrupt, revert stage/clear/commit, cancel active run.
7. **Export check** — the same review-note limitation as the journey.

### Deferred rendering

A control the installed version does not support is rendered as **deferred**, not hidden and not fabricated. Examples: separate tool catalog, provider quota, live formatter/LSP health. The reason is visible in the capability grid and in `docs/OPENCODE_INTEGRATION.md`.

## Visual tokens

The existing haunted-workshop palette is retained:

- background `#111018`, surface `#1b1824`, raised `#252031`;
- text `#f4f0e8`, muted `#b8afca`;
- accent `#f4b66c`, spirit `#bfa3ff`, success `#8bd5a7`, danger `#ffb4a8`;
- Georgia for headings, system sans for UI, monospace for technical metadata;
- 16px cards, 12px controls, 44px minimum action height.

New components reuse these tokens rather than introducing a second design language.

## Accessibility

- Onboarding is a labelled region; diagnostics are a list with text, not color alone.
- State pills include the state word, so color is supplementary.
- The advanced panel uses native disclosure semantics.
- Inputs have visible labels; the password field has a specific description.
- Focus remains a 3px solid outline plus a `box-shadow` ring for browsers that report outline style inconsistently.
- Reduced-motion preference disables the lantern flicker and seal fade.
- `prefers-contrast: more` strengthens borders; forced-colors keeps buttons and the lantern usable.
- The layout stacks at narrow widths; long model IDs, URLs, diagnostics, and diffs wrap rather than overflow.

## Error and recovery copy examples

| Situation | Copy |
|---|---|
| Password mismatch | “OpenCode rejected the application connection. Enter the same password printed by `opencode serve`.” |
| No models | “OpenCode returned no selectable models. Connect a provider inside OpenCode with `/connect`, then retry.” |
| Unavailable model | “The selected model is no longer reported by OpenCode. Choose another model; the previous selection was not replaced automatically.” |
| Unsupported variant | “Variant `max` is not attached to this model. Reported variants: low, medium, high.” |
| Local limits | “This local model reports a small context/output window. Reduce scope or choose a model with larger limits. OpenCode does not report free RAM or VRAM.” |
| Origin/proxy | “A proxy or origin rule rejected the server-side request. Browser CORS is not required because the app connects from its own process.” |
| Restart during run | “The application restarted while this native run was in flight. Reconcile the OpenCode session before another attempt.” |

## What not to do

- Do not put provider-key inputs anywhere.
- Do not put model or connection controls in the main document.
- Do not show a fixed model name in marketing copy or a default chip.
- Do not claim a run passed, a model is free, or a quota is available without an observed value.
- Do not auto-approve a permission request.
- Do not automatically switch a project to a different model when the saved one disappears.

This document is the sole canonical future implementation plan. `docs/ENGINEERING_BLUEPRINT.md` remains the authoritative legacy blueprint and execution record until deliberate migration in Phase 9, but it must not receive new roadmap claims in place of the canonical documents below.

## Baseline gate

The repository baseline was verified on Node `22.14.0`, npm `10.9.2`, installed OpenCode CLI `2.0.32`, and code HEAD `2205774012160d8355a3a7f22ebc37de27fd558f`.

Clean-install and verification sequence:

```bash

```

Phase 0 proved the typecheck, 22-test suite, production build, and safe preflight. Phase 1 passes typecheck and 42 deterministic tests, including the asynchronous run API, event stream, restart recovery, native interrupt, timeout, failure classification, redaction, verification, and schema migration/backup. The production build passes with the existing large-chunk warning, and preflight exits 0 as `PREFLIGHT_ONLY`. The existing user state was inspected read-only as schema v1/revision 6 before implementation; tests use temporary fixtures and no local application startup or live inference was performed.

## Proposed target architecture

The run coordinator/event journal path is implemented in Phase 1. The remaining shell, mode policy, catalog, and fixture branches are future state:

```text
Browser shell
  |-- stable workflow navigation and OpenCode onboarding
  |-- Run Inspector over server-sent events
  |-- deterministic demo adapter using production schemas
  v
Server/API
  |-- durable run coordinator + event journal + native interruption/reconcile
  |-- capability/mode policy (local full | hosted demo | private hosted)
  |-- versioned catalog + deterministic recommendation rules
  |-- versioned migrations, backups, retention, limits, and recovery
  v
OpenCode boundary (full modes only)       Fixture boundary (demo mode only)

# Decisions

Status: canonical append-only decision log  
Last verified: 31 October 2026 (IST)

Decisions describe durable constraints and their consequences. Future work belongs in [IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md](IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md). When a decision changes, add a superseding entry; do not silently rewrite historical rationale.

## ADR-001 — OpenCode is the only coding harness

- Date: 31 October 2026
- Status: accepted
- Context: Unfinished Business needs native sessions, model/provider access, permissions, tools, edits, diffs, and execution lifecycle without implementing a second agent loop.
- Decision: OpenCode is the only product coding harness. The application may add orchestration, workflow approvals, evidence, UI, policy, and recovery around OpenCode, but it must not add Codex, Claude Code, Copilot, Backboard R-CLI, Mastra, or another harness as an interchangeable runtime.
- Consequences: Provider credentials remain owned by OpenCode; integration changes must follow OpenCode's supported APIs; version-specific gaps are documented rather than replaced with a parallel executor. Backboard, Sentry, and Entire may provide partner evidence or observability but are not coding-harness alternatives.

## ADR-002 — Separate local full, hosted demo, and private hosted deployment

- Date: 31 October 2026
- Status: accepted direction; mode implementation is deferred to Phases 6–7
- Context: A browser-accessible demo and a full coding environment have different credential, filesystem, cost, and isolation requirements.
- Decision:
  - **Local full execution** is the primary path for real OpenCode sessions and edits under the user's local trust boundary.
  - **Hosted demo** will be a deterministic, quota-free, clearly disclosed experience that does not expose live provider credentials or unrestricted code execution.
  - **Private hosted deployment** may run full execution only for an operator-controlled instance with its own authentication, secrets, persistent storage, backup, cost, and isolation responsibilities.
- Current reality: the checked-in Render blueprint is a private single-service full-execution shape protected by one HTTP Basic Auth credential. It is not a public hosted demo, has not been deployed or externally verified in Phase 0, and is not claimed as multi-user isolation.
- Consequences: No public page may silently invoke a live model or write to a shared workspace. A browser-to-local tunnel remains deferred until separately approved with pairing, loopback defaults, HTTPS, origin allowlists, scoped short-lived tokens, revocation, and visible connection state.

- Date: 31 October 2026
- Status: accepted
- Context: The repository contains a detailed legacy blueprint, idea packet, setup/deployment guides, runtime prompts, and a new phased roadmap. Duplicating all content immediately would create contradictory plans.
- Decision: The ownership table in [IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md](IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md) assigns one canonical owner per subject. Phase 0 creates only owners needed for baseline facts and policy. Legacy documents stay in place, and `docs/ENGINEERING_BLUEPRINT.md` remains authoritative legacy content until the Phase 9 line-by-line migration.
- Consequences: Later phases update the canonical owner in the same change as implementation. README and prompt indexes link rather than duplicate. No legacy file is archived or deleted before Phase 9 proves its unique facts and stable links are preserved.

## ADR-004 — Persisted schema changes are forward-only and backup-first

- Date: 31 October 2026
- Status: accepted; schema v2 implementation completed in Phase 1
- Context: The current project record is schema v1 with only a one-generation `.previous` snapshot and no migration runner.
- Decision: Every durable schema change uses explicit sequential forward migrations and a verified, uniquely named backup before replacement. Unsupported newer state fails closed; corrupt input is preserved; migration performs no network or inference work.
- Consequences: A phase cannot claim a schema change complete until migration fixtures, interruption/corruption recovery, backup validation, and rollback limits satisfy [OPERATIONS_AND_RECOVERY.md](OPERATIONS_AND_RECOVERY.md).

## ADR-005 — Maker uses a bounded in-process coordinator

- Date: 31 October 2026
- Status: accepted
- Context: The current product is one Node process with file-backed state and one OpenCode server. Durable Maker identity and restart safety are required, but a distributed workflow service would add an unneeded deployment and trust boundary.
- Decision: Save each run and its native identifiers in schema-v2 project state, then execute through a concurrency-bounded in-process coordinator (default one). On restart, reconcile non-terminal runs against OpenCode and never automatically resend the prompt.
- Consequences: Browser refresh and application restart preserve run identity and evidence. Execution does not continue inside a stopped Node process, multi-instance writers are unsupported, and operators must not point concurrent processes at one data directory. A different coordinator requires a later ADR and migration plan.

## ADR-006 — Run progress uses authenticated resumable SSE

- Date: 31 October 2026
- Status: accepted
- Context: Run progress is server-to-browser, ordered, and read-mostly. The product already uses HTTP and does not need bidirectional transport for Phase 1.
- Decision: Expose the append-only run journal through workshop-token-authenticated server-sent events with event sequence ids, cursor/`Last-Event-ID` resume, invalid-cursor snapshot resync, heartbeat, and terminal closure.

# Operations and recovery

Status: canonical state, backup, migration, and recovery policy  
Last verified: 31 October 2026 (IST)

This document owns persisted-state operations. Phase 1 implements the first forward migration and durable run recovery; the remaining hardening limits are explicit below.

## Current persisted state

`UB_DATA_DIR` defaults to `.unfinished-business/`. The application currently manages:

```text
UB_DATA_DIR/
  project.json
  project.json.previous
  project.json.backup-v1-<timestamp>-<checksum>.json
  project.json.backup-v1-<timestamp>-<checksum>.json.manifest.json
  demo-workspace/
  spirit-workspace/
```

Render additionally keeps OpenCode XDG data and config under `/var/data`. Secrets remain environment-owned and are not part of a repository backup.

`project.json` uses `schemaVersion: 2` and a monotonically increasing `revision`. Its validated record contains the schema-v1 workflow fields plus `runs`: durable Maker identity/state, OpenCode session and message references, cancellation intent, a versioned append-only event journal, failure classification, and terminal evidence.

Normal saves remain temporary-file-plus-rename writes with a one-generation `.previous` copy. Loads fall back to `.previous` when the primary file cannot be parsed or validated. A later save from fallback preserves the corrupt primary under a unique `.corrupt-<timestamp>` name before replacing it.

Phase 0 validated the existing local primary record read-only as schema v1/revision 6 and the previous snapshot as schema v1/revision 5. Phase 1 implementation and tests did not start the application against that directory, so the user-owned records were not migrated during this work. The next real startup with Phase 1 code will perform the documented v1-to-v2 backup and migration.

## Versioning rules

1. `schemaVersion` is a required positive integer at the root of every durable project record. Version 2 is the current implemented version; version 1 is the supported migration source.
2. A code change that changes required fields, field meaning, enum meaning, identity, or durable invariants must increment the schema version. Adding a Zod default alone does not waive migration review.
3. Migrations are forward-only, explicit, deterministic functions `N -> N+1`. `migrateProjectV1` is the implemented `1 -> 2` step and validates both source and result.
4. A migration must preserve ids, approvals, hashes, revisions, evidence provenance, operation/native-session references, and user text unless the corresponding decision entry explicitly documents a loss and recovery path.
5. Unsupported newer versions fail closed with an actionable message. They must never be coerced into an older schema or overwritten.
6. Migration code performs no inference, network requests, provider login, deployment action, or external account mutation.
7. Every migration requires fixtures and backup/result validation. Phase 1 proves successful v1 migration and corrupt-input fallback but does not yet claim cross-process locking or injected interruption-at-every-write-step testing; those are Phase 8 hardening obligations.

## Backup-before-migration rules

The implemented v1-to-v2 path performs the following before replacement:

1. Startup reaches the store before the HTTP listener accepts mutations. There is no separate cross-process data-directory lock, so two processes must not share one `UB_DATA_DIR`.
2. It reads and validates the schema-v1 source bytes without modifying them.
3. It creates a uniquely named timestamp/checksum backup of `project.json` with exclusive creation semantics.
4. It records source/target schema, source and backup paths, creation time, and SHA-256 in a secret-free manifest.
5. Verify the backup can be read before migration continues.
6. It writes and re-validates the migrated record in a unique temporary file, then atomically renames it into place.
7. It does not automatically prune migration backups. Restore and deletion remain explicit operator actions.

The Phase 1 migration backup covers the primary project record only. It does not yet snapshot `.previous`, workspaces, or OpenCode XDG metadata, and it does not fsync files/directories explicitly. Operators of a private hosted instance should also take a provider disk snapshot. Phase 8 owns full-directory consistency and retention.

## Forward migration and rollback

- Startup may automatically migrate only versions explicitly listed as supported by the running build. It must surface that a backup and migration occurred.
- If any step fails, leave the original and backup untouched, quarantine partial output, and refuse mutations. Do not initialize a blank project over recoverable data.
- Rollback means stopping the application and restoring a verified pre-migration backup with the application version that understands it. Never run older code against state already written by newer code.
- A successful migration is not reversed in place. Corrections are a new forward migration.
- OpenCode session ids may outlive application migration but are external references; inability to inspect an old session must become an honest limitation, not deletion of local evidence.

## Current recovery matrix

| Symptom | Safe current action | Do not do |
|---|---|---|
| `project.json` invalid but `.previous` valid | Stop writes, copy both files to an operator backup, inspect the load source, and restore deliberately. | Do not delete the primary or assume fallback is a migration. |
| Both project files invalid | Preserve both and logs, stop the app, and diagnose against the declared schema version. | Do not let startup replace them with a new project. |
| Revision conflict | Reload project state and reapply the user's intended change to the new revision. | Do not bypass the expected revision. |
| Duplicate action id/same payload | Treat the returned state as the idempotent result. | Do not invoke OpenCode again. |
| Duplicate action id/different payload | Generate a new action id after reviewing intent. | Do not reuse the id or overwrite its ledger entry. |
| Run `UNKNOWN` with session id | Use Run Inspector reconciliation; it inspects the saved OpenCode session and resumes observation/evidence collection without prompting again. | Do not start a duplicate run merely because the browser disconnected or the local wait expired. |
| Run `UNKNOWN` without session id | Review the event explaining where creation was lost. A new run is allowed only after accepting that native outcome cannot be inspected. | Do not fabricate failure/success or assume no native work occurred. |
| Maker is running after browser refresh | Reopen the saved run; SSE resumes from the browser cursor or snapshot resync. | Do not submit Maker again. |
| Server restarts with a non-terminal run | Startup reconciles the saved native session. Running work is observed; terminal work is finalized; missing references become `UNKNOWN`. | Do not automatically retry or resend the prompt. |
| Cancellation requested | Wait for OpenCode interruption confirmation. `CANCELLED` means the native session reported interruption; uncertainty means `UNKNOWN`. | Do not equate a local button click or network response loss with native cancellation. |
| OpenCode unavailable/auth failure | Correct the server URL/password outside persisted project state, then re-probe. | Do not store provider/server secrets in `project.json` or browser storage. |
| Sentry unavailable | Continue local operation and record telemetry as unverified. | Do not treat lack of telemetry as proof that no failure occurred. |

## Event retention and evidence

- Run events are append-only within `project.json`; sequence numbers are per run and never reused. Phase 1 performs no pruning. This is suitable for the current single-user/local scale but unbounded growth is a known limitation.
- The Run Inspector renders the most recent 50 events while the complete journal remains persisted and available to SSE snapshot/replay.
- Terminal run results retain file summaries and bounded verification output, not file contents or native tool output. OpenCode remains the native source for deeper session history while it is retained there.
- Migration backups are retained indefinitely by application code. Operators must not delete the last verified pre-migration backup; a safe rotation policy is deferred to Phase 8.

## Phase obligations

- Phase 1 implements durable in-flight runs, native interruption, restart reconciliation, append-only event retention, and backup-first schema v2 migration.
- Phase 6 documents and verifies mode-specific backups and resets for local full, hosted demo, and private hosted deployments.
- Phase 8 completes locking, backup rotation, corruption quarantine, retention, incident response, budgets, secure cleanup, and recovery tests.
- Phase 9 exercises supported prior-version fixtures and links release evidence.

# Decisions

Current decisions for the OpenCode connection, discovery, and supported-control phase. Older decisions remain in the [engineering blueprint](ENGINEERING_BLUEPRINT.md) and idea packet as historical records.

## D-20 — OpenCode remains the only coding harness

**Decision.** The application does not add a second agent loop, provider client, tool executor, or command runner. It calls the OpenCode server through the exact `@opencode/client` version and keeps product roles as adapters.

**Reason.** The product value is the workshop, staged approvals, and evidence. Rebuilding execution would duplicate permission and recovery logic.

## D-21 — Discovery replaces the fixed DeepSeek assumption

**Decision.** Models, providers, limits, modalities, tool support, reasoning variants, and availability come from the OpenCode catalog. The project stores the chosen model and each operation/evidence row records the model used.

**Reason.** A fixed model becomes wrong when a catalog changes, a provider is removed, or a user chooses another supported model. The fixed identity remains only as a migration hint.

**Consequences.** A user must choose a model when the catalog has one. If the saved model disappears, the app reports `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` and does not silently substitute.

## D-22 — Variants are model-reported, never a universal scale

**Decision.** Only variant IDs returned for the selected model are selectable. “Model default” means no explicit variant. The app does not invent low/medium/high for a model that does not report them.

**Reason.** OpenCode documents that variant names come from the selected model's current catalog metadata and unknown variants fail model resolution.

## D-23 — Provider keys never enter Unfinished Business

**Decision.** The application has no provider-key field, route, log field, browser storage key, project field, or export field. The only credential it accepts is the OpenCode server Basic-auth password.

**Reason.** OpenCode owns provider authentication. Duplicating it creates a second secret store and a new leak surface.

**Consequences.** The wizard asks only for the server password. Unknown credential-shaped request fields are rejected. Hosted deployments configure provider accounts inside OpenCode or its environment.

## D-24 — The OpenCode server password is memory-only in the wizard

**Decision.** A password entered in the wizard is held in the application process. `connection.json` stores URL, auth mode, username, and a “password previously configured” flag, never the password. Non-interactive deployments use `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` from their secret store.

**Reason.** It avoids a new on-disk secret format while keeping local first-run usable. A restart can require re-entry; that is an honest state, not a silent auth failure.

**Consequences.** After a restart without `OPENCODE_PASSWORD`, the next check returns `authentication_required`. The UI says the process no longer holds the password.

## D-25 — Connection checks are read-only

**Decision.** A check calls `/api/info`, catalogs, agents, permissions, commands, skills, MCP, and config. It does not prompt a model, edit a session, or change provider state. The live diagnostic may create/get/remove one empty session; it never prompts.

**Reason.** “Connected” must not imply inference succeeded or a paid request occurred.

## D-26 — Remote URLs require HTTPS; loopback may use HTTP

**Decision.** `http://` is limited to `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and `::1`. Other hosts must be `https://`. Credentials in a URL are rejected.

**Reason.** A server password over plaintext remote HTTP is unacceptable. The app connects server-side, so browser CORS is not a reason to weaken this rule.

## D-27 — Session actions are project-scoped

**Decision.** The session API lists and acts only on sessions referenced by the active project. It does not enumerate every OpenCode session. Fork/compact/revert/interrupt require that ownership check.

**Reason.** A shared OpenCode instance may contain other projects' sessions. A browser control must not become a cross-project administration surface.

## D-28 — Maker runs are asynchronous and persisted

**Decision.** `POST /api/runs` returns `202` after persisting a `QUEUED` operation and starting the in-process runner. Completion is written against the latest project revision. A restart converts in-flight runs to `UNKNOWN`; cancellation cannot be overwritten by a late completion.

**Reason.** The Phase 1 prerequisite required a non-blocking, non-lossy run model. Holding an HTTP request for a multi-minute model turn loses the request on a proxy timeout and hides progress.

## D-29 — Unsupported controls are deferred visibly

**Decision.** The installed version's gaps are rendered as deferred with a reason. In `2.0.32`: no separate HTTP tool catalog; no provider quota; formatter/LSP is configuration presence only; fork requires a non-empty session.

**Reason.** “Not supported” is a product state, not a reason to guess an endpoint or fabricate a capability.

## D-30 — Deployment modes are explicit

**Decision.** `local`, `hosted-private`, and `hosted-demo` have different connection-edit and credential rules. Hosted modes manage the connection through environment/secret stores and expose read-only connection UI. The public demo never asks visitors for provider keys.

**Reason.** A shared hosted instance must not turn a browser visitor into the owner of the OpenCode server or provider account.

## D-31 — Version policy is major-compatible with tested-patch warnings

**Decision.** Accept OpenCode major 2; warn/degrade on a patch other than `2.0.32`; reject other majors. Record the tested version in the integration document and expose it through the live diagnostic.

**Reason.** The HTTP contract is versioned by major, but optional fields and controls can drift within a major. A warning is more honest than claiming untested compatibility.
# Changelog

All notable changes to Unfinished Business. Dates are local execution dates.

## Unreleased — Phase 2

### Added

- OpenCode connection state model: `not_configured`, `checking`, `connected`, `authentication_required`, `incompatible_version`, `unavailable`, `degraded`.
- First-run wizard for server URL, Basic-auth username/password, connectivity test, provider readiness, model choice, reported variants, and harmless verification.
- Provider/model discovery normalization: display names, pricing/free/paid, local status when known, context/input/output limits, modalities, tool support, reasoning support source, variants, availability.
- Expandable OpenCode panel: model/variant selection, agents and explicit role mapping, pending permissions, commands, skills, MCP servers, formatter/LSP configuration, project-scoped sessions, usage.
- Model selection persisted in project schema v2; Maker records the selected model in its operation and evidence.
- Migration from v1 fixed-model projects to v2 with a legacy hint that is used only when the model is still reported.
- Project-scoped session list/resume/interrupt/fork/compact/revert and permission replies.
- Opt-in live compatibility diagnostic: `npm run diagnose:opencode`.
- Deployment modes: `local`, `hosted-private`, `hosted-demo`.
- Actionable diagnostics for password mismatch, provider auth, unavailable/disabled/unreported models, unsupported variants, unsupported server version, origin/proxy rejection, local model limits, and process restart.

### Changed

- Replaced the hard-coded free DeepSeek model with the discovered `engine` selection.
- `POST /api/runs` now returns `202` immediately and the browser polls persisted state. The run manager records `QUEUED`/`RUNNING`/terminal states, model, agent, and timestamps.
- Background project updates use latest-revision retry; store writes are serialized and use UUID temp names.
- Cancellation interrupts the native session and cannot be overwritten by a late completion.
- Process restart converts in-flight operations to `UNKNOWN` for explicit reconciliation.
- Provider credentials are never accepted by the application; only the OpenCode server password is accepted (memory-only in the wizard).
- Active setup docs and README no longer instruct users to require a fixed model.

### Tests

- Non-blocking run lifecycle, completion, failure, duplicate action, cancellation, and inactive-run behavior.
- URL policy, version policy, auth failure/recovery, provider/model normalization, secret redaction, local-limit diagnostics, managed-mode lock.
- v1 → v2 migration and persistence.
- Model/variant validation and onboarding HTTP flow.
- Project-scoped session authorization and actions.
- Onboarding browser end-to-end flow against a mock `2.0.32` OpenCode server.
- Full suite: 55 tests pass; typecheck and production build pass.

### Deferred

- Separate tool catalog (not exposed by OpenCode `2.0.32`).
- Provider quota/balance (not exposed by the HTTP API).

## Phase 1 prerequisite — asynchronous runs

The project previously committed the foundation, durable workflow, and guided workshop experience. /home/kernel-kain/Documents/Github/unfinished-business/.entire/metadata/01a191a7-2b24-7c62-a012-d93074e6cc14/full.jsonl:335:{"timestamp":"2026-10-31T11:17:58.974Z","ordinal":334,"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":"01a191a7-2b24-7c62-a012-d93074e6cc14","turn_id":"01a191a7-cc4f-70d1-b474-a5288f9b0c41","item":{"type":"AgentMessage","id":"msg_0e98fcd4b4c31f7e016ae5ce3bd20481919313fa084e83326d","content":[{"type":"Text","text":"# Implementation plan

I audited the repository and produced the roadmap below without changing any files, packages, images, deployments, credentials, or commits. The current baseline is healthy: type-checking passes and all 22 tests pass.

The product should become:

> An OpenCode-powered hackathon project builder that turns an unfinished idea into an approved plan, bounded implementation, verified evidence, and submission-ready demo.

OpenCode remains the only coding harness. Other tools are recommendations for projects created with Unfinished Business—not competing harnesses inside the product.

## What the audit found

The Maker problem is architectural rather than cosmetic:

- The frontend waits for one long synchronous request and only shows a warning after eight seconds in [App.tsx](/home/kernel-kain/Documents/Github/unfinished-business/src/web/App.tsx:50).
- The backend records the operation only after OpenCode returns in [service.ts](/home/kernel-kain/Documents/Github/unfinished-business/src/server/experience/service.ts:82).
- OpenCode can run for up to 180 seconds without streaming visible progress in [guide.ts](/home/kernel-kain/Documents/Github/unfinished-business/src/server/experience/guide.ts:95).
- Cancel currently changes the saved status but does not interrupt the OpenCode session.
- The fixed model is hard-coded in [client.ts](/home/kernel-kain/Documents/Github/unfinished-business/src/server/opencode/client.ts:4).
- All four stage buttons are disabled, so users cannot inspect future or completed stages.
- Activity shows only four truncated results rather than a live execution trace.
- Local saved state contains repeated `Authentication required` failures, confirming that OpenCode onboarding must come before Maker.
- The project is currently single-workspace and single-user. Turning the public Render deployment into a shared multi-user filesystem agent would be unsafe without substantial isolation.

The uncommitted user changes in [ENGINEERING_BLUEPRINT.md](/home/kernel-kain/Documents/Github/unfinished-business/docs/ENGINEERING_BLUEPRINT.md:1) and `.backboard/` must be preserved during implementation.

## Product and experience direction

Use the positioning:

> “Finish your hackathon project with a guided OpenCode workflow.”

The four characters become functional guides, not decorative mascots:

| Guide | Purpose | Visual direction |
|---|---|---|
| Oracle | Clarifies the idea, audience, constraints, and success criteria | Spectral seer with a lantern orb |
| Architect | Creates the architecture, contracts, scope, and test strategy | Blueprint spirit with compass and animated construction lines |
| Maker | Runs bounded OpenCode implementation work | Friendly mechanical ghost with tool belt, sparks, and build states |
| Witness | Verifies evidence and prepares the demo and submission | Archival moth/eye spirit with scan beam and approval stamp |

Theme: **Ghostlight Hacker Workshop**—deep navy and ultraviolet shadows, amber workbench light, terminal glow, layered blueprint cards, subtle glass and paper textures, and restrained 2.5D depth.

Animations should communicate state:

- Idle, listening, thinking, working, blocked, success, and error poses.
- Motion-powered card transitions, line drawing, parallax, progress pulses, and success stamps.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` alternatives.
- No heavy WebGL or continuously animated backgrounds that hurt performance.

The landing background should later be generated as a wide 21:9 image: a spectral hackathon workshop with an unfinished robot, terminal, blueprints, and four subtle spirits; dark navy/indigo with amber highlights, no text or logos, and quiet space behind the headline. Produce AVIF/WebP variants with a dark overlay and mobile crop. It has intentionally not been generated yet.

## Phased implementation roadmap

### Phase 0 — Protect the baseline and reorganize the plan

- Capture the current behavior, screenshots, routes, state schema, and failure modes.
- Preserve the existing dirty files.
- Decide the supported OpenCode version and pin compatibility to that version.
- Create a state-schema migration strategy before changing persisted project data.
- Define one canonical product brief, one engineering plan, and one decision log.
- Mark old documents as historical rather than silently overwriting them.

Acceptance:

- Existing projects still load.
- Current tests remain green.
- Every future phase has explicit documentation and migration requirements.

### Phase 1 — Fix Maker reliability first

Replace the long synchronous request with an asynchronous run lifecycle:

1. `POST /api/runs` immediately saves a `QUEUED` run and returns `202 { runId }`.
2. A runner creates the OpenCode session and saves its session ID before prompting.
3. The run moves through `QUEUED → CONNECTING → RUNNING → WAITING_FOR_PERMISSION → VERIFYING → SUCCEEDED/FAILED/CANCELLED/UNKNOWN`.
4. Subscribe to OpenCode events and normalize them into persisted run events.
5. Stream events to the UI using SSE with event cursors and reconnect support.
6. Refreshing the page reconnects to the existing run.
7. Cancel invokes OpenCode’s session interrupt endpoint.
8. A timeout becomes `UNKNOWN` or still-running—not a discarded session.
9. Reconciliation checks OpenCode before allowing a retry.
10. Double-submit protection prevents duplicate Maker runs.

The new Run Inspector should show:

- Connection and session creation.
- Selected model and reasoning variant.
- User-visible model updates.
- Tool calls with secrets redacted.
- Permission requests.
- Files inspected and changed.
- Diff summary.
- Commands and test results.
- Elapsed time, context use, tokens, and cost where exposed.
- Recovery, retry, interrupt, and final evidence.

Do not expose hidden chain-of-thought. Show operational events and concise model-authored progress summaries.

Acceptance:

- First progress appears within 500 ms.
- Maker never appears frozen.
- Refresh resumes the trace.
- Cancel actually stops the OpenCode run.
- The session ID is never lost on timeout.
- A terminal run contains a diff, verification evidence, and clear next action.

### Phase 2 — Proper OpenCode onboarding and harness controls

OpenCode already exposes server, provider, model, session, permission, event, command, skill, MCP, and agent surfaces. The product should use these APIs rather than rebuilding them independently. [OpenCode server documentation](https://docs.opencode.ai/docs/server/), [provider setup](https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/), [models and variants](https://opencode.ai/docs/models), and [agents](https://docs.opencode.ai/docs/agents/) cover the relevant primitives.

Build a first-run connection wizard:

1. Detect whether OpenCode is reachable.
2. Explain how to install/start OpenCode locally.
3. Verify server URL and authentication.
4. Direct the user through OpenCode’s own provider connection process.
5. Fetch providers, models, capabilities, agents, and defaults.
6. Run a harmless connection test.
7. Save only connection metadata—not raw provider credentials.
8. Show repair instructions for authentication, missing models, unsupported tools, and version mismatch.

Expose contextually:

- Provider and model picker.
- Free, local, promotional, or paid status.
- Context/input/output limits.
- Tool, image, and reasoning support.
- Reasoning variants supported by the chosen model.
- Usage, context, tokens, and cost when OpenCode/provider data provides them.
- Agent selection and four project-specific agents.
- Permission policies: allow, ask, or deny.
- Pending permission requests.
- Sessions: list, resume, fork, compact, revert, interrupt, and export.
- Commands, skills, MCP servers, LSP, formatters, and tool availability.

Do not hard-code provider quota numbers; they change. Link users to provider billing or usage pages and display live facts only when available.

OpenCode-only boundaries:

- No Codex, Claude Code, Copilot, or alternate harness selection in the UI.
- Models from multiple providers are allowed only through OpenCode.
- Provider SDKs are not called directly by the core app.
- Backboard, Mastra, and similar services may be recommended for a generated project, but they do not replace OpenCode internally.

### Phase 3 — Navigation, outlines, and project information architecture

Make all four character tabs selectable at all times:

- Completed tabs are reviewable.
- The active stage is editable.
- Future tabs show prerequisites, expected output, and a preview.
- Mutation buttons remain locked until prerequisites are satisfied.
- Store the selected tab in the URL.
- Add “Return to active task” and a persistent workflow status header.

Replace technical section titles with user-facing names while retaining stable internal IDs:

1. Vision & Success
2. Architecture
3. User Experience
4. OpenCode Setup
5. Tools & Budget
6. Validation
7. Build Roadmap
8. Demo & Launch

Every section card should include:

- Status and owner.
- Short summary.
- Dependencies.
- Last update.
- Stale reason.
- Edit/review action.
- Source evidence or related run.

Add a project dashboard containing readiness, blockers, current run, budget, tool recommendations, demo status, and submission checklist.

### Phase 4 — Landing page and visual redesign

Landing page sections:

1. Hero: “Turn unfinished ideas into hackathon-ready builds.”
2. Primary actions: try the example, connect OpenCode, or set up locally.
3. Two usage modes.
4. Four-character workflow.
5. Interactive example.
6. OpenCode feature preview.
7. Idea-to-tool recommendation preview.
8. Local setup commands.
9. Privacy and security explanation.
10. Evidence/test philosophy.
11. FAQ.
12. Final CTA.

Interface improvements:

- Layered panels with shadow, texture, lighting, and depth.
- Stronger typography and section hierarchy.
- Responsive navigation and mobile run inspector.
- Skeletons and stage-specific progress states.
- Actionable empty, error, authentication, and timeout states.
- Consistent button hierarchy.
- Keyboard navigation, visible focus, WCAG contrast, reduced motion.
- Animated characters kept outside essential reading and interaction paths.

### Phase 5 — Tool recommendation engine

The app should recommend tools based on the user’s idea, not show a sponsor wall.

Extract idea attributes such as:

- Web application
- AI inference or fine-tuning
- Tabular data
- Hardware
- Voice
- Browser automation
- Authentication
- Search
- Durable workflows
- Time-series data
- Remote database
- Public deployment

Each recommendation should show:

- Why it fits.
- Open-source/free/promotional status.
- Free allowance and important limits.
- Local or hosted setup.
- License.
- Estimated integration effort.
- Whether it helps a challenge category.
- Privacy or lock-in warning.
- “Add to plan” action—never automatic installation.

### Tool filter for a solo hackathon builder

| Tool | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Render | Include conditionally. Free services work for a stateless demo, but free instances do not support the persistent disk this app currently uses. A reliable personal deployment will likely be paid. [Render free limits](https://render.com/docs/free) |
| TabPFN | Recommend only for tabular classification/regression ideas. Free/open-weight for appropriate non-commercial use, subject to its model license. |
| Tinker | Promotional/conditional. Useful for model fine-tuning, but not a free ongoing default. |
| Arduino | Recommend for hardware ideas. Tooling and many designs are open source, but physical hardware costs money. [Arduino licensing](https://support.arduino.cc/hc/en-us/articles/4415094490770-Licensing-for-products-based-on-Arduino) |
| DigitalOcean | Promotional only. Cloud credit is useful, but it is not a permanently free platform. |
| Gemma | Strong recommendation for local/open-weight AI through OpenCode and Ollama. |
| Auth0 for AI Agents | Conditional. Proprietary free tier; valuable only when the generated project needs user identity, delegated tool authorization, or multiple users. [Auth0 pricing](https://auth0.com/pricing) |
| Backboard | Promotional/conditional for memory or model routing. Do not use its CLI as the internal harness because the product is OpenCode-only. |
| ElevenLabs | Optional for speech and voice demos. Proprietary free tier with quota and usage restrictions. [ElevenLabs pricing](https://elevenlabs.io/pricing) |
| Browserbase | Recommend Stagehand locally first; its core is open source. Browserbase’s hosted browser service has a small free allowance. [Browserbase pricing](https://www.browserbase.com/pricing), [Stagehand](https://github.com/browserbase/stagehand) |
| Entire | Strong recommendation and already enabled. Useful for preserving agent work, provenance, and recoverable sessions. [Entire pricing](https://entire.com/pricing) |

### Phase 1 — Fix Maker reliability first

Replace the long synchronous request with an asynchronous run lifecycle:

1. `POST /api/runs` immediately saves a `QUEUED` run and returns `202 { runId }`.
2. A runner creates the OpenCode session and saves its session ID before prompting.
3. The run moves through `QUEUED → CONNECTING → RUNNING → WAITING_FOR_PERMISSION → VERIFYING → SUCCEEDED/FAILED/CANCELLED/UNKNOWN`.
4. Subscribe to OpenCode events and normalize them into persisted run events.
5. Stream events to the UI using SSE with event cursors and reconnect support.
6. Refreshing the page reconnects to the existing run.
7. Cancel invokes OpenCode’s session interrupt endpoint.
8. A timeout becomes `UNKNOWN` or still-running—not a discarded session.
9. Reconciliation checks OpenCode before allowing a retry.
10. Double-submit protection prevents duplicate Maker runs.

The new Run Inspector should show:

- Connection and session creation.
- Selected model and reasoning variant.
- User-visible model updates.
- Tool calls with secrets redacted.
- Permission requests.
- Files inspected and changed.
- Diff summary.
- Commands and test results.
- Elapsed time, context use, tokens, and cost where exposed.
- Recovery, retry, interrupt, and final evidence.

Do not expose hidden chain-of-thought. Show operational events and concise model-authored progress summaries.

Acceptance:

- First progress appears within 500 ms.
- Maker never appears frozen.
- Refresh resumes the trace.
- Cancel actually stops the OpenCode run.
- The session ID is never lost on timeout.
- A terminal run contains a diff, verification evidence, and clear next action.

# Local setup

This guide starts from a clean checkout on Linux. OpenCode is the only coding harness; Unfinished Business adds the workshop UI, staged approvals, evidence, and connection/discovery controls.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js `22.14` or newer and npm.
- A terminal on the same machine as the workshop.
- OpenCode `2.x`; the tested version is `2.0.32`.

The repository pins the matching client and Linux baseline CLI:

```bash
npm ci
```

## 1. Start OpenCode

```bash
opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096
```

If `opencode` is not on `PATH`, install it using the official method for your platform:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash
```

OpenCode prints a server password. Keep it out of the repository. The workshop uses it only for its own server-side Basic-auth connection.

For a disposable check without touching your normal OpenCode state, use temporary XDG directories:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/ub-opencode
XDG_DATA_HOME=/tmp/ub-opencode/data \
XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/ub-opencode/config \
XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp/ub-opencode/cache \
XDG_STATE_HOME=/tmp/ub-opencode/state \
OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD='choose-a-local-password' \
opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096
```

## 2. Check the OpenCode surface (optional)

From the repository:

```bash
OPENCODE_LIVE_DIAGNOSTIC=1 \
OPENCODE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4096 \
OPENCODE_PASSWORD='the same server password' \
npm run diagnose:opencode
```

This connects, lists the catalog, and creates/reads/removes one empty session. It performs no prompt or model inference. Without the opt-in flag it prints `SKIP`.

## 3. Start Unfinished Business

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173`. Vite proxies `/api` to the application server on `UB_PORT` (default `4200`). For the built app:

```bash
npm run build
npm start
```

Then open `http://127.0.0.1:4200`.

Configuration is read from a gitignored `.env`; use `.env.example` as the safe template:

```dotenv
OPENCODE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4096
# Optional for interactive local use. The wizard can hold it in memory instead.
OPENCODE_PASSWORD=
UB_PORT=4200
UB_HOST=127.0.0.1
UB_DATA_DIR=.unfinished-business
UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=local

# Product brief

**Unfinished Business — Bring your ideas to life.**

A local browser workshop on top of OpenCode. Four friendly spirits guide a builder from an unfinished idea to an approved plan, one bounded implementation, inspected evidence, and honest demo/submission drafts.

## Audience and problem

The primary user is a first-time hackathon builder or developer using AI who has a vague idea or a stalled attempt. They need help deciding what to ask, which capability to use, how to carry decisions between sessions, and whether the result is actually ready.

The product coordinates intent, decisions, execution, and evidence. It does not replace OpenCode's agent loop, model access, tools, permissions, or sessions.

## The four-stage journey

| Stage | User-facing role | Completed when |
|---|---|---|
| **Oracle** | Clarify the idea and approve a useful product scope. | The user explicitly approves an Oracle proposal. |
| **Architect** | Review and approve one project section at a time. | Every required section is approved and no stale decision remains. |
| **Maker** | Grant separate execution scope, run the approved unit through OpenCode, and inspect the real result. | A durable Maker run succeeds with a diff and evidence, or its limitation is explicit. |
| **Witness** | Review evidence and prepare findings, limitations, and draft notes. | Drafts are ready for review; publication and submission remain separate. |

The stages are sequential workflow roles, not four simultaneous agents. A stage becomes active only through persisted workflow state.

## Inspect every stage, mutate only the active one

All four spirit tabs are selectable at any time:

- **Completed stages** show approved artifacts, versions, approvals, and observed evidence.
- **The active stage** shows its permitted actions.
- **Future stages** show purpose, prerequisites, expected output, and a preview.

Selecting a tab is a **view** action. It never approves a section, grants execution scope, starts a run, or changes the active stage. The selected tab is stored in the URL as `?view=oracle`, `?view=architect`, `?view=maker`, or `?view=witness`, so a view is shareable and survives reload without changing workflow state. Direct navigation is not authorization.

The active stage is always visible in a badge. A **Return to active task** action is available from every other tab. The interface states plainly when the user is reviewing a completed stage or previewing a future one.

## Project sections

The plan uses eight stable internal identifiers with clear user-facing labels. Labels may change; approvals and content hashes stay attached to the same record.

| # | Label | Internal id | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Vision & Success | `control` | — |
| 2 | Architecture | `architecture` | `control` |
| 3 | User Experience | `experience` | `control`, `architecture` |
| 4 | OpenCode Setup | `tools` | `architecture` |
| 5 | Tools & Budget | `readiness` | `control`, `architecture`, `tools` |
| 6 | Validation | `verification` | `control`, `architecture`, `tools` |
| 7 | Build Roadmap | `phases` | `verification` |
| 8 | Demo & Launch | `delivery` | `experience`, `verification`, `phases` |

`readiness` is the historical internal id for the Tools & Budget area. Existing v1/v2 records migrate their labels, order, and dependency edges without changing ids, content, versions, hashes, statuses, or approvals.

Each section card shows:

- status and readiness (`ready`, `draft`, `approved`, `stale`, `locked`, or `blocked`);
- a concise summary and owner;
- dependencies and whether each is approved;
- version and last update;
- stale reason when an upstream change invalidated the approval;
- the exact approval record and an evidence link;
- one clear edit, review, or locked action.

## Project overview

The overview is the persistent answer to "where am I?" It shows:

- overall readiness and stage progress;
- active blockers with the stage they belong to;
- the current or latest durable run, including `UNKNOWN` outcomes;
- OpenCode connection state and the first repair diagnostic;
- model pricing status and bounded tool availability;
- demo status from evidence and Witness drafts;
- the exact next action.

Partial, stale, blocked, loading, and recovery states are first-class. Connection failures and unresolved runs are never hidden behind navigation.

## Terminology

- **Active stage** — the workflow role the server permits to act.
- **Selected tab** — the stage the user is viewing.
- **Completed / active / future** — the relationship of a selected tab to the active stage.
- **Ready** — dependencies are approved and the section can be reviewed.
- **Stale** — an upstream change invalidated a previous approval; review and reapprove it.
- **Locked** — dependencies are not approved, so the section cannot be drafted.
- **Blocked** — dependencies are approved, but an earlier section still needs a decision.
- **Approval** — an exact section version and hash, persisted by the application.
- **Execution scope** — a separate, explicit permission for Maker; plan approval is not execution permission.

## Boundaries

- OpenCode owns provider credentials, models, tools, permissions, native sessions, and execution.
- Unfinished Business owns the workshop, staged approvals, dependency invalidation, selected-view navigation, project overview, and evidence references.
- The application never accepts provider API keys and never stores the OpenCode server password in project data or browser storage.
- A native denial cannot be overridden by a product approval.
- A successful run or a model statement is not proof of a passing check.
- Witness drafts are in-app review notes, not a published article, video, or submitted entry.
- Hosted execution, multi-user collaboration, and automatic publication are outside the first release.

## Related documents

- [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) — implemented components and the selected-view/workflow-state boundary.
- [UX and visual system](UX_AND_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md) — navigation, section anatomy, states, responsive behavior, and accessibility.
- [Operations and recovery](OPERATIONS_AND_RECOVERY.md) — schema migration, stale/blocked recovery, and run reconciliation.
- [Implementation plan](IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md) — phase status and next prerequisite.
- [Decisions](DECISIONS.md) — durable product and architecture choices.
